A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same KnowFREE research framework. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables and figures, are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial additions and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original Chinese NER, segmentation and POS-tagging experiments, component ablations, and appendix studies of LLM labeling and data synthesis.

after.justification: v3 retains original empirical results and adds multilingual evaluations, full-dataset experiments, additional ablations and synthetic-data LoRA comparisons.

M1.justification: v1 specifies a fixed extension-label loss weight, alpha=0.13. v3 Appendix H introduces label-frequency-dependent weights, alpha_i=0.5*Cbar/C_i, changing the training-loss procedure. The two enhancement pipelines, biaffine/local-attention architecture and inference masking remain substantially unchanged.

E1.justification: The eight Chinese datasets are retained. v3 adds English NER on CoNLL’03 and MIT-Movie, Japanese NER on Stockmark-NER, and Korean NER on Naver Changwon NER. These evaluations substantially broaden represented languages and domains.

E2.justification: v3 adds MELM and brings CNN Nested NER and DiFiNet into the few-shot comparison alongside LLM-DA and ProgGen. Appendix A adds Llama3-8B to zero-shot and LoRA comparisons, and Llama3.1-70B and DeepSeek-V3 to zero-shot comparisons. The conventional comparator set in Table 1 remains unchanged.

E3.justification: v3 adds full-dataset training, synthetic-data LoRA experiments, and Llama3.1-70B, GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3 augmentation configurations. It reports beta=0.4 for several retained NER datasets versus v1’s uniform 1.0. The attention-head study changes its stated augmentation model from GLM3-6B to GLM4-9B-Chat and extends the tested configurations. These reported changes do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 Table 3 adds removal of both local attention and label extension, plus replacement of local attention with masked CNNs. Appendix D extends head-count sensitivity testing through 14 heads. Appendix A adds source-only versus synthetic-augmented LoRA comparisons and discusses overprediction errors. The earlier t-SNE and label-logit analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 Table 2 adds standard deviations alongside few-shot scores; v1 reports point estimates only. This is a limited uncertainty-reporting addition: neither version specifies repeated-run counts or seeds, and v3 does not establish an increase in repetitions.

E6.justification: v3 adds substantial few-shot, multilingual, full-data and LLM results. Eleven retained Table 1 entries also change; for example, GLM4 fusion-only Weibo at 1000 samples changes from 72.01 to 72.59. Conventional-baseline scores remain unchanged. Because loss settings are also revised, these numerical revisions do not establish controlled same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Appendix H introduces Equation 15, formally defining frequency-dependent extension-label weights absent from v1. The existing clustering, attention and loss mathematics otherwise remain equivalent or are condensed into prose. Neither version contains theorem or proof developments.

C1.justification: v3 broadens the empirical applicability claim beyond Chinese: the introduction explicitly includes English, and the abstract and conclusion remove the Chinese-only qualification. The central contributions—extension-label fusion, contextual explanation synthesis and inference without external features—remain unchanged.

C2.justification: v3 adds explanations of synthetic-data LoRA failures through spurious co-occurrence and non-target overprediction, discusses full-data applicability and attention-head computational tradeoffs, and emphasizes benefits from larger augmentation LLMs. Its dedicated Limitations section largely restates v1’s existing warning that synthetic-data noise can outweigh benefits as data increases.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code-access link and substantially expands implementation documentation in Appendix H: separate learning rates of 2e-5 and 1e-3, dataset-specific weight decay and beta settings, Transformers implementation, and two NVIDIA A6000 GPUs. Existing encoder dimensions, clustering thresholds and attention defaults are relocated rather than newly introduced.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion adds InstructUIE, UniversalNER and GoLLIE, while synonymous-label handling is connected to surface-form competition. Additional references support MELM, newer LLMs, datasets and implementation software. The central positioning relative to span-based labeling and LLM augmentation remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 extensively rewrites the introduction around model-centric and data-centric approaches, condenses the method exposition, and reorganizes results into many-shot and few-shot subsections. It moves the t-SNE analysis into the main text and training details into Appendix H, standardizes variant names, and adds Limitations and Ethics sections.

P2.justification: v3 adds a conceptual comparison as Figure 1, incorporates the earlier illustrative example into a substantially expanded Figure 2, and redraws Figure 3 to clarify inference masking. Table 1 changes from two dataset panels to one wide table, several result tables are added, and the retained t-SNE visualization moves into the main text.

improvement.justification: The new attention-removal and CNN-replacement ablations directly test a contribution whose benefit v1 inferred mainly from comparisons between different models. Multilingual and full-data evaluations substantially strengthen evidence about applicability, while uncertainty reporting and implementation details improve assessability. These gains outweigh remaining reporting weaknesses: run counts are unspecified, and revised loss settings are not reconciled with retained scores.
